approachQuestion.prompt:
Rain Basin
A rectangular grid of nonnegative ground heights receives unlimited rain. Water flows between side-adjacent cells and can leave through any boundary cell to the outside. Return the total retained water volume, one unit of area per cell. Example: [[5,5,5],[5,1,5],[5,5,5]] → 4; [[5,0,5],[5,1,5],[5,5,5]] → 0.

1 ≤ R,C ≤ 500; 1 ≤ R*C ≤ 200000; heights are integers from 0 to 1000000000. Input is read-only. Total volume fits signed 64 bits. A grid without an interior cell retains zero water. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 1 ≤ R,C ≤ 500; 1 ≤ R*C ≤ 200000; heights are integers from 0 to 1000000000. Input is read-only. Total volume fits signed 64 bits. A grid without an interior cell retains zero water.

options.text: Mark each distinct boundary cell visited and insert it in a min-heap keyed by its height. Remove the smallest effective boundary height h. For each unvisited side neighbor of ground g, mark it visited, add max(0,h−g) to volume, and insert that neighbor with effective height max(h,g). Continue until the heap is empty.
options.feedback: The smallest current escape barrier is finalized first. A newly reached cell cannot drain below that barrier through any unprocessed route, so its effective height is the greater of its ground and that barrier. Boundary seeding accounts for every way water can escape.

options.text: For every interior cell separately, run a minimum-barrier path search to any boundary, then add the positive difference between that minimum possible path-maximum height and the cell’s ground.
options.feedback: This computes the right escape level for each cell but repeats nearly the same global search from every interior location.

options.text: For each interior cell, use the minimum of the maximum ground in its row in each direction and its column in each direction as the water level.
options.feedback: Winding escape paths are missed. In [[5,0,5,5,5],[5,1,1,1,5],[5,1,1,1,5],[5,1,1,1,5],[5,5,5,5,5]], all interior ground-1 cells drain through the top opening, but the center’s four straight directions all see height 5.

options.text: Use the boundary min-heap process, but insert a reached neighbor with its raw ground g instead of max(h,g).
options.feedback: In a 4×4 grid with boundary height 5 and four interior cells of height 1, inserting raw 1 lets later interior cells appear to drain below the surrounding wall and undercounts the required volume 16.

The lowest effective frontier is the next escape boundary. A neighbor retains water up to that boundary and propagates max(boundary,ground), not its raw height alone. Mark on insertion to avoid charging one cell repeatedly.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A with a binary min-heap of (effectiveHeight,row,column) and an R-by-C boolean visited array. Let M=R*C. Insert each boundary cell once even at corners. Each cell is marked when enqueued and every heap repair is iterative; no grid copy or hash table is used. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(M log(M+1)) time, O(M) auxiliary space
O(M² log(M+1)) time, O(M) auxiliary space
O(M log(M+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Every grid cell enters and leaves the frontier heap once, with four neighbor checks.
details: Every cell enters and leaves the heap exactly once; there are at most four neighbor checks per removal. Binary-heap repairs on variable-size frontiers give O(M log(M+1)) worst-case time. The visited array alone requires O(M), as does the largest possible heap. Ground remains in the input and the returned volume is scalar. Grids with no interior still perform the specified boundary processing; there is no early-return shortcut in this fixed method.
“O(M) time, O(M) auxiliary space”: The neighbor checks are linear, but the binary-heap ordering work is additional.
“O(M² log(M+1)) time, O(M) auxiliary space”: That repeated-search bound describes the per-cell alternative; A shares a single boundary expansion.
“O(M log(M+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Visited flags and queued frontier records are counted as workspace.
